$comment: Rule catalog — innovation. The single source of machine truth for rule identity and metadata. A policy may select a different LEVEL for a project; it may never redefine what a rule means, and it may never invent a rule this file does not define. Seven rules here are invariant-class — both `forbidden` and `nonExemptible` — and a failure of any of them yields BLOCKED_BY_INVARIANT rather than ordinary non-compliance (ADR 0005). Every rule below `full` assurance carries an $assuranceNote stating in words what its check does NOT establish; most innovation rules are `partial` because the presence of a section is mechanically checkable and the adequacy of its content is not.

rules.title: Innovation decisions are recorded in a proposal artifact at the canonical path
rules.description: A decision to build, defer, reject, or otherwise dispose of an idea is recorded as a structured proposal at artifacts/innovation-proposals/NNNN-<kebab-slug>.md, carrying the required sections.
rules.rationale: A decision that exists only in a conversation cannot be reviewed, cited, revisited, or checked. The artifact is what makes innovation discipline auditable at all.
rules.remediation: Copy templates/innovation-proposal.md into artifacts/innovation-proposals/ as NNNN-<kebab-slug>.md and complete the required sections.

rules.title: The problem is stated before the solution
rules.description: The proposal records what is wrong, who is affected, and why it matters now, before it proposes anything.
rules.rationale: A solution presented without a problem is a preference, and the strength of the argument for it is unrelated to whether anyone needs it.
rules.remediation: Complete the Problem section: Statement, Who is affected, and Why it matters now.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that the three fields are present and non-empty. It CANNOT establish that the stated problem is real, that the named affected party exists, or that 'why now' describes a genuine change. A problem statement reading 'users are frustrated' satisfies this check.

rules.title: Building is never recommended without an identified problem
rules.description: A proposal whose outcome is build or prototype must not have an absent or empty problem statement.
rules.rationale: A recommendation to build something whose problem was never identified has no basis, and every estimate, design, and schedule downstream of it inherits that.
rules.remediation: Identify the problem, or change the outcome to explore — which is the outcome for work that is still searching for one.
rules.$assuranceNote: Invariant-class: failure yields BLOCKED_BY_INVARIANT. Establishes that a build or prototype outcome is accompanied by a non-empty problem statement. It CANNOT establish that the problem is genuine. Applicability is conditional on the recorded outcome.

rules.title: Every evidence entry carries a level from the closed taxonomy
rules.description: Each evidence entry is written as `- **En [level]** claim`, where level is one of observation, assumption, hypothesis, user-evidence, market-evidence, technical-evidence, experiment-result, validated-conclusion.
rules.rationale: A claim with no level is not a weaker claim but an unclassifiable one, and unlabelled prose makes an intuition indistinguishable from twelve interviews.
rules.remediation: Label every evidence entry with a level from the closed set.

rules.title: Evidence citations resolve
rules.description: A (source: path) citation to a repository-relative path names a file that exists, and a (from: En) citation resolves to an entry in the same proposal.
rules.rationale: A citation to something that does not exist is the cheapest form of fabricated evidence, and the only form a machine can catch.
rules.remediation: Correct the path or the entry reference, or record the claim at the level its actual support justifies.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that repository-relative citation targets exist and that entry cross-references resolve. URLs and absolute paths are skipped rather than guessed at. It CANNOT establish that a cited document says what the entry claims it says.

rules.title: Evidence levels are never silently upgraded
rules.description: A validated-conclusion entry cites the specific entries that support it, and those citations do not resolve solely to assumptions or hypotheses.
rules.rationale: An upgrade with no citation is a change of adjective rather than a change of evidence, and a chain terminating in nothing observed is not validation however many steps it has.
rules.remediation: Cite the supporting entries with (from: E1, E3), or record the claim at the level its support justifies.
rules.$assuranceNote: Invariant-class: failure yields BLOCKED_BY_INVARIANT. Establishes that a validated-conclusion carries citations and that they do not resolve solely to assumption or hypothesis entries. It CANNOT establish that the cited evidence actually supports the conclusion — that is human review.

rules.title: Market validation, customer feedback, and metrics are never fabricated
rules.description: No recorded evidence is invented, including plausible-sounding user quotes, market sizes, or metrics generated rather than retrieved.
rules.rationale: Fabricated evidence does not make a proposal incomplete; it makes every conclusion resting on it invalid, and worse than one with no evidence at all because it forecloses the enquiry that would have found the truth.
rules.remediation: Remove the fabricated entry and record what is actually known at its true level. Where evidence is needed and absent, the outcome is validate or insufficient-evidence.
rules.$assuranceNote: Invariant-class: failure yields BLOCKED_BY_INVARIANT. NO automated check evaluates this rule. Nothing mechanical distinguishes a real interview from an invented one. Without a human attestation it reports not-evaluated, which means nobody looked — not that nothing was wrong.

rules.title: Assumptions and uncertainty are declared
rules.description: The proposal records the assumptions it rests on and the material things it does not know.
rules.rationale: An unknown that is omitted has not been resolved; it has been made harder to raise, because there is no longer a place in the document where raising it is expected.
rules.remediation: Complete the Assumptions and uncertainty section with at least one assumption or unknown.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that the section exists with at least one entry. It CANNOT establish that the assumptions recorded are the ones that matter, or that a material uncertainty has not been omitted.

rules.title: Novelty and AI approval are not evidence of value
rules.description: That something is new, technically interesting, or considered good by an AI is not recorded or relied upon as evidence of its value.
rules.rationale: That something has not been done before is a fact about the past, not a claim about demand — often it has not been done because it is not worth doing. A model's confidence supports nothing.
rules.remediation: Replace the appeal to novelty or model approval with evidence at a level from the taxonomy, or record the honest outcome of explore.
rules.$assuranceNote: NO automated check evaluates this rule. Whether technical interest was the real motivation is not visible in the text of a document written to obscure it. Without a human attestation it reports not-evaluated.

rules.title: Existing capability is searched, and the search is recorded
rules.description: The proposal records which projects, products, or capabilities were examined and what was found in each.
rules.rationale: A search that was not performed must not be reported as a search that found nothing; the two are written identically in careless prose and are completely different claims.
rules.remediation: Complete the Existing capability section: Searched, and Finding.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that both fields are present and non-empty. It CANNOT establish that the search was wide enough, that the capabilities named exist, or that the stated reason an existing capability does not solve the problem is true.

rules.title: Alternatives include doing nothing, building, buying, and integrating
rules.description: The Alternatives section names all four of Do nothing, Build, Buy, and Integrate, each with a substantive answer. A non-viable alternative is recorded with the reason it is not viable.
rules.rationale: Do-nothing is the baseline every other option is measured against, and building is the option whose costs are most familiar to the proposal's author and least visible to its approver.
rules.remediation: Complete all four alternatives. Where one is not viable, record why.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that all four named fields are present and non-empty. It CANNOT establish that the alternatives were genuinely evaluated. A field reading 'Buy: not viable' with no reasoning satisfies this check and fails the standard.

rules.title: User value, expected impact, differentiation, and alignment are stated
rules.description: The proposal states what changes for the affected party, the impact expected if it succeeds, what distinguishes it from what exists, and how it aligns with portfolio strategy.
rules.rationale: Real problems of no consequence are common; establishing that a problem exists is a separate question from establishing that solving it is worth something.
rules.remediation: Complete the Value and alignment section: User value, Expected impact, Differentiation, Strategic alignment.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that the four fields are present and non-empty. It CANNOT establish that stated value is real, that an impact estimate is plausible, that a differentiation claim would survive contact with the competitor, or that alignment prose is anything other than generic. This section is the one most likely to be written persuasively by a language model and least likely to be checked.

rules.title: Cost is accounted across every dimension that will be paid
rules.description: The proposal records implementation complexity, maintenance burden, operational burden, opportunity cost, and technical debt.
rules.rationale: Maintenance and operational burden are paid indefinitely and largely by people who were not in the room when the proposal was approved.
rules.remediation: Complete the Costs section: Implementation, Maintenance, Operational, Opportunity cost, Technical debt.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that the five named fields are present and non-empty. It CANNOT establish that an estimate is realistic, or that a cost known to the author has not been omitted — that omission is the subject of innovation.no-hidden-costs, which is human review.

rules.title: Major implementation or maintenance costs are never hidden
rules.description: A cost the author knows about is recorded, whether or not it weakens the case. Costs that cannot be estimated are recorded as unknown at their true uncertainty rather than left blank.
rules.rationale: A known cost that is omitted is a misrepresentation of the proposal, not an oversight of detail, and the decision it produces was made on information the decider did not have.
rules.remediation: Record the omitted cost and re-evaluate the decision against it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Invariant-class: failure yields BLOCKED_BY_INVARIANT. NO automated check evaluates this rule. Nothing mechanical can know what the author knew and did not write down. Without a human attestation it reports not-evaluated.

rules.title: Security and privacy implications are stated
rules.description: The proposal states what data it would touch, what new exposure it would create, and which existing standards and obligations apply to it.
rules.rationale: Security and privacy consequences are cheapest to address before the design is chosen and most expensive after the system holds real data.
rules.remediation: Complete the Security and privacy section: Implications, and Applicable standards.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that both fields are present and non-empty. It CANNOT establish that the analysis is correct or complete, and it is not a security review. A dedicated review is a different activity performed by different people.

rules.title: Novelty confers no exemption from any applicable standard
rules.description: An idea is not exempted from security, privacy, engineering, financial, legal, or any other applicable standard on the grounds that it is innovative, experimental, a prototype, or a pilot.
rules.rationale: 'It is only a prototype' is the phrase that carries production data into an unreviewed system, and the exemption is claimed exactly when the safeguards are most needed.
rules.remediation: Apply the standard. Where it genuinely does not apply, record why under its own applicability mechanism rather than by appeal to novelty.
rules.$assuranceNote: Invariant-class: failure yields BLOCKED_BY_INVARIANT. NO automated check evaluates this rule; this repository cannot see the other standards a project is subject to. Without a human attestation it reports not-evaluated.

rules.title: A release objective is recorded
rules.description: The proposal records a single statement of what the release is for, against which any later scope change is visible as a change.
rules.rationale: Scope may change; it must never change silently. Without a recorded objective there is no baseline against which drift can be detected.
rules.remediation: Record the Release objective field in the Scope and MVP section.

rules.title: A minimum viable definition and an out-of-scope list are recorded
rules.description: The proposal records what would minimally satisfy the release objective, and what is deliberately excluded.
rules.rationale: An explicit out-of-scope list is what makes a later inclusion a visible decision rather than a drift nobody chose.
rules.remediation: Complete the MVP and Out of scope fields in the Scope and MVP section.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that both fields are present and non-empty. It CANNOT establish that the MVP is actually minimal, or that the out-of-scope list names the things most likely to creep in.

rules.title: The release objective is never changed silently
rules.description: A change to the recorded release objective is accompanied by a visible revision entry stating what changed and why. Scope may change; it may not change without leaving a trace.
rules.rationale: A release objective rewritten in place converts a decision someone approved into a different decision they did not, and nothing in the resulting document reveals the substitution.
rules.remediation: Record the change as a revision entry with its date and reason, and re-confirm the decision against the new objective.
rules.$assuranceNote: NO automated check evaluates this rule. Detecting a silent change requires comparing against history, which this tooling does not read — an objective rewritten before commit leaves nothing in the file to find. Version control is the residual control, and it is a control only if someone reads the diff. Without a human attestation this reports not-evaluated.

rules.title: Success criteria are observable and recorded in advance
rules.description: The proposal records at least one success criterion, stated in terms observable by someone who did not write the proposal.
rules.rationale: Criteria written after the outcome is visible measure nothing; recording them in advance is what makes the later comparison meaningful.
rules.remediation: Add at least one Criterion to the Success criteria section, expressed as something observable.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that at least one criterion is present. It CANNOT establish that a criterion is measurable, that it relates to the stated problem, or that it was written before the result was known — the last is not visible in the file at all.

rules.title: Kill criteria are recorded and can fire
rules.description: The proposal records at least one observable condition under which the work would stop.
rules.rationale: A decision to start with no defined conditions for stopping is a decision to continue indefinitely, and the cost of that is paid quietly.
rules.remediation: Add at least one Criterion to the Kill criteria section, with an observable trigger.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that at least one criterion is present in a section distinct from Success criteria. It CANNOT establish that the criterion has a real threshold, a named observer, or any possibility of firing.

rules.title: Effort already spent is never the reason to continue
rules.description: A decision to continue is justified by whether the remaining work is worth its remaining cost, judged from where the work now stands, and never by the investment already made.
rules.rationale: Money and effort already spent are gone under every option, so they cannot discriminate between options; treating them as a reason converts a bad decision into a permanent one.
rules.remediation: Re-evaluate the proposal from its current state, disregarding prior investment, and record the outcome that analysis supports.
rules.$assuranceNote: Invariant-class: failure yields BLOCKED_BY_INVARIANT. NO automated check evaluates this rule; the reasoning behind a continuation is not mechanically recoverable. Without a human attestation it reports not-evaluated.

rules.title: An experiment precedes a build where it would resolve the decisive uncertainty more cheaply
rules.description: A proposal deciding to build carries at least one experiment-result, user-evidence, or technical-evidence entry, or states why an experiment would not have reduced the decisive uncertainty.
rules.rationale: Where an experiment would answer the question for a fraction of the cost of building, building first buys the same information at a much higher price and with a commitment attached.
rules.remediation: Run the experiment and record its result, or record why the uncertainty could not be resolved more cheaply than by building.
rules.$assuranceNote: The only recommended-level rule in this catalog, because whether an experiment should precede a build depends on the cost of the build and the degree of uncertainty — a judgement the tooling cannot make. Establishes only that a build decision rests on at least one entry above hypothesis level. Applicability is conditional on the recorded outcome.

rules.title: Exactly one outcome from the closed set is recorded
rules.description: A decided proposal records one outcome drawn from explore, validate, prototype, build, defer, reject, merge-with-existing, insufficient-evidence.
rules.rationale: No outcome is privileged: a properly evidenced decision not to build is as compliant as a properly evidenced decision to build, and a closed set is what makes that comparable across a portfolio.
rules.remediation: Record one Outcome in the Decision section, drawn from the closed set.

rules.title: A suspended decision records the condition that revives it
rules.description: A proposal whose outcome is defer or insufficient-evidence records a RevisitWhen condition. A proposal with any other outcome does not need one.
rules.rationale: A suspension with no revisit condition is indistinguishable from something that was forgotten, and the two have very different consequences.
rules.remediation: Record a RevisitWhen condition naming the observable event that should reopen the decision.

rules.title: Undecided ideas are never presented as commitments
rules.description: An idea that has been generated but not decided is not presented, aggregated, scheduled, or reported as though it carried commitment.
rules.rationale: Generated ideas are cheap and plentiful under AI assistance; a list of them formatted as a roadmap creates expectations nobody agreed to and capacity nobody has.
rules.remediation: Separate the idea inventory from the committed work, and mark undecided items as undecided wherever they are presented.
rules.$assuranceNote: NO automated check evaluates this rule; how an idea is presented outside the proposal is not visible to this tooling. Without a human attestation it reports not-evaluated.

rules.title: Overlap, duplication, and cannibalization are addressed
rules.description: The proposal records what it overlaps with in the existing portfolio, what it would duplicate, what it would cannibalize, and its priority relative to other work.
rules.rationale: Two efforts solving one problem is a portfolio defect whether or not either effort is individually sound, and neither proposal will notice it alone.
rules.remediation: Complete the Portfolio section: Overlap, Cannibalization, Priority.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that the fields are present and non-empty. It CANNOT establish that the author was right about the overlap. NO cross-repository or cross-portfolio scan exists in this tooling; the check verifies that the question was addressed, never that the answer is correct.

rules.title: Prioritization discriminates
rules.description: A priority scheme in which everything is a priority is not used, and a proposal's stated priority is meaningful relative to other work.
rules.rationale: A priority scheme that does not discriminate conveys no information and defers the real decision to whoever is loudest at the moment of execution.
rules.remediation: Rank the work against the rest of the portfolio so the priority distinguishes this proposal from others.
rules.$assuranceNote: NO automated check evaluates this rule; judging whether a priority discriminates requires the whole portfolio, which this tooling does not see. Without a human attestation it reports not-evaluated.

rules.title: A new project justifies its separation against all eight considerations
rules.description: A proposal of type new-project answers each of existing project ownership, duplicated infrastructure, duplicated domain logic, maintenance cost, deployment cost, support burden, fragmented user experience, and portfolio complexity.
rules.rationale: A new project faces a higher bar than new functionality because the burden of proof falls on separation, and every cost of separation is paid indefinitely by people who were not in the room.
rules.remediation: Complete all eight fields in the New project justification section, or change the proposal type — the outcome for a capability an existing project should own is merge-with-existing.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that all eight named fields are present and non-empty. It CANNOT establish that the answers are honest or that the separation is warranted. Applicability is conditional: the rule applies if and only if the recorded proposal type is new-project.

rules.title: The standards system is never weakened to permit a desired conclusion
rules.description: No standard, test, applicability determination, evidence requirement, or verification mechanism is bypassed, weakened, removed, reclassified, reinterpreted, falsified, or manipulated solely because it prevents a desired implementation or conclusion.
rules.rationale: An AI agent optimising for a clean verdict has an incentive to modify whatever is preventing task completion, and the cheapest route to green runs through defeating the check rather than satisfying it.
rules.remediation: Restore the rule, test, or determination to its defined form and address the underlying finding. A standard may be revised for good reasons through a visible, reasoned, recorded change — but never solely because it obstructs a desired conclusion.
rules.$assuranceNote: Invariant-class: failure yields BLOCKED_BY_INVARIANT. Establishes two mechanically visible forms: a policy declaring a rule below the level the catalog defines, and an exception filed against an invariant-class rule. It CANNOT establish intent, and it CANNOT prevent an actor with write access from editing a rule, a detector, or a test. What the mechanism provides is that such an edit is visible in the verdict, the test suite, and version history — not that it is impossible.
